findings.title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` setting row exists
findings.body: The `execute(...)[0]['id']` call indexes the first row of a join between `categories` and `site_settings` on `name = 'embed_category'`. On any install where that setting was never saved, the result set is empty, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The `category_id == 0` fallback below it is never reached. The same problem applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15, whose `[0]['value']` is also unguarded. The migration needs to handle empty results.

findings.title: Raw string interpolation in INSERT; host values are unquoted, unstripped and unnormalised
findings.body: Each line of the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is interpolated straight into SQL as `'#{h}'`. A value containing a quote breaks or injects into the statement. Lines are also not stripped, so `\r` or whitespace can be inserted. They are not normalised either: old entries like `http://foo.com` are stored with the scheme, and the model's `before_validation` stripping is bypassed. Use `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote` or the model, and strip and normalise each entry.

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a controller request with a missing `host` param gives nil, so it raises instead of failing validation. The in-place `sub!` also mutates the attribute string. Guard with `host.present?` or use non-bang `sub` with assignment.

findings.title: update/destroy use `.first` and dereference nil for unknown ids
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing or already-deleted id. `save_host(nil)` and `host.destroy` then raise NoMethodError and the client gets a 500. Use `find`, which gives a proper 404, or add an explicit not-found response. `save_host` also dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without a guard when the param is absent.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the input
findings.body: The query is `lower(host) = ?` with `uri.host` passed through unchanged. If the referer or URL host has uppercase characters (for example `http://EvilTrout.com/`), it will never match and the embed is rejected. Downcase the input (`host.downcase`). `record_for_host` also returns `false` instead of nil on failure, which is inconsistent with the `first` result.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between category and embeddable_host files
findings.body: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category` and `:private_category` fabricators. It works only because both files are loaded, but it is clearly a mix-up. It will confuse anyone looking up a fabricator by filename and invites future conflicts or duplicate definitions.

findings.title: Test no longer verifies host-dependence and its name is misleading
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer checks for any embeddable host, so 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. It no longer tests what its name says. The removed host check is a behaviour change, and the new test does not cover it.

findings.title: `update` action is a no-op that returns the current state
findings.body: `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` ignores all params and just re-serializes. The client `saveChanges` action calls `update({})`, so it implies saving but does nothing. Either remove the route and action, or implement them.

findings.title: New admin CRUD endpoints have no functional tests
findings.body: Both new controller specs only assert inheritance from `AdminController`. Create, update, destroy, validation errors, default category fallback, and non-admin access are all untested. The nil-id and nil-param crash paths would have been caught.

findings.title: `_ids` embedding assumes an array and can leave undefined entries
findings.body: The regex `(.+)\_id(s?)$` now matches any key ending in `_ids`, and `obj[k].map` throws if the value is not an array (null or a string). Entries that `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve become `undefined` inside the hydrated array. The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code, since `map` always returns an array.
